overview.body:
**Angrboða** ​(*angrboda*) — ‌Monster ‌Mother, ​Sorcery · ​She ​who offers ​sorrow ​— belongs ‌to ​the ​Norse tradition, ‌where ​it is ‌catalogued ​under the ‌domain ​"Monster ​Mother, Sorcery". ​The ​name means ​"She ‌who ​offers sorrow"[^1].

‌**Angrboða** ​belongs to ‌the ​Norse tradition, ‌where ​it ‌is associated ​with ​monster mother, ‌sorcery.[^2]

‌PuniCodex restores ‌the ​name ​as **Angrboða** ‌and ​serves its ​temple ‌at ​[angrboda.com](https://punicodex.com/angrboda/). The ​restoration ‌preserves at ​least ‌one distinctive ​feature ​— ​a diacritic ​or ‌a distinctive ‌letter ​— ‌that the ​ASCII ​form loses, ‌and ‌exactly one ‌historically ‌valid ​Unicode restoration ‌exists, ​which places ​the ​name in ‌Tier ​1. ​The plain ​ASCII ‌form *angrboda* ​survives ​as ​a modern ‌convenience ​imposed by ‌the ​early domain-name ‌system; ​the ‌restoration, not ‌the ​fallback, is ​the ​form the ​project ‌defends ‌as philologically ​complete[^3].

the-name.body:
The name ​is attested ‌in Younger ‌Futhark as ​**ᛅᚾᚴᚱᛒᚢᚦᛅ**. Etymologically ​it means ​"She who ​offers sorrow"[^1].

​Old Norse ‌Angrboða, from ​angr 'sorrow, ​grief' + ‌boða 'to ​offer, to ‌announce'; mother ​of Fenrir, ‌Jörmungandr, and ​Hel by ​Loki.

The ​ASCII form ​*angrboda* survives ​only because ‌the early domain-name ​system could ‌not carry ​diacritics; it ‌is a ​technological compromise, ‌not an ​ancient spelling. ‌The Unicode ​restoration **Angrboða** ​recovers the ‌full diacritic ‌detail of ‌the scholarly ​transliteration directly ​in the ‌address bar. ​The restoration ​preserves at ‌least one ​distinctive feature ​— a ‌diacritic or a ​distinctive letter ‌— that ​the ASCII ​form loses, ​and exactly ​one historically ‌valid Unicode ‌restoration exists, ​which places ‌the name ​in Tier ​1.

The ‌letter-by-letter transformation ‌runs:

- ‌**a** → ‌**A** — ​Same, capitalized
‌- **n** ​→ **n** ​— Same
​- **g** ‌→ **g** — ​Same
- ​**r** → ​**r** — ‌Same
- ​**b** → ​**b** — ​Same
- ‌**o** → ​**o** — ‌Same
- ​**d** → ‌**ð** — ​Eth: voiced ‌dental fricative
‌- **a** ​→ **a** ​— Same

​The canonical ​temple for ‌this name ‌is served ​at **angrboda.com**[^2].

pronunciation.body:
The ​reconstructed ‌pronunciation ‌of ​the ​name is ​**/angrboda/** ​— ​Norse ‌Reconstruction.[^1]

​Phoneme ​by ‌phoneme:

​- ‌**A** ​— Initial ‌character ​of ​the ​restored ​form ​Angrboða.
‌- ​**ngrboða** ‌— Remainder ​of ‌the ​name, ‌preserving ​the ‌distinctive ​marks ​of ‌the ‌Norse tradition.

‌For ​the ​modern ‌speaker, ​the ​closest ‌approximation ​is: ​'ANGRBODA' ‌— pronounce ​the ‌restored ​form ​with ​attention ​to ‌the ‌preserved ​diacritics ‌and length.

​Kindred ​and ‌historical ‌forms ‌of ‌the ​name:

‌- ​**Norse** ​— Angrboða, ​the ‌restored ​Unicode ​form ​of ‌the ​name

​Angrboða ​is Tier ‌1 ​because ‌the ​Norse ‌form ​preserves ‌distinctive ‌features ​that ​ASCII loses: ​stress, ​length, ‌or ‌special ​characters.

mythology.body:
The ​stories of ‌**Angrboða** ‌circulate within ​the ​Norse corpus, ​where ​the figure ​embodies monster ‌mother, ​sorcery.[^1]

### ​Primary ‌Attestation (Sources)

​Angrboða ‌is attested ​in ‌the canonical ​Norse ​sources as ​a ​figure associated ​with ‌monster mother, ​sorcery.[^2]

### ‌Name ​and Meaning ‌(Etymology)

​The name ‌means ​"She who ‌offers ​sorrow" and ​reflects ‌the figure's ‌role ‌in the ​tradition. ​**Angrboða** is ‌a jötunn ​of ​the Iron ‌Wood ​and the ​mother ‌of three ​monstrous ‌children by ​Loki: ​Fenrir, Jörmungandr, ​and ​Hel. Her ‌name, "She-Who-Offers-Grief," ‌signals ​her role ‌in ​the coming ​Ragnarök.[^1] ‌The Prose ‌Edda ‌presents her ‌as ​the source ‌of ​the forces ​that ​will unmake ‌the gods, ​yet ​she remains ​a ‌marginal, barely ​narrated ​figure. Some ​modern ‌readings interpret ​her ‌as the ​land's ‌ancient, ungovernable ​fertility, ‌producing the ‌very forces ​that ​will consume ​the ​cosmic order ‌established ‌by the ​Æsir.[^2]
